ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Power of Friendliness / How to Make Effective Slides

fullPassage:
It's good to see you, everyone! I'm Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It's fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need. Now, this raises some interesting questions: where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important? To answer these questions, I'd like to tell you about my childhood companion dog, Sparky. When we played with a ball, I noticed that he responded well to my gestures.
The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
I'll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
Now let's turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
A successful presentation relies on employing various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures, making natural eye contact, and speaking with an appropriate volume. But just as important, well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively conveying your message. Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to focus more on listening than on reading. Next, prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally achieved with a font size of at least 18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides with high-quality images that complement the text. By following these simple tips, you can create effective slides that hold your audience's interest and keep them engaged from start to finish!

questions.passage: It's good to see you, everyone! I'm Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. On my way, I had trouble ①<u>locating</u> this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and ②<u>walked</u> me here. It's fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in ③<u>need</u>. When we played with a ball, I noticed that he responded ④<u>good</u> to my gestures.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④good→well: 동사 responded를 수식하려면 부사 well이 필요. good은 형용사.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ good → well: responded(동사)를 수식하는 부사 필요
❌ ① locating: have trouble ~ing 구문 올바름
❌ ② walked: walk + 목적어 + 장소 '걸어서 데려가다' 올바름
❌ ③ need: 'someone in need' = 도움이 필요한 사람, 명사 올바름
det.tip: good(형용사) vs well(부사): 동사를 수식할 때는 부사 well. have trouble ~ing = ~하는 데 어려움을 겪다

questions.passage: He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures ①<u>compared</u> to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food ②<u>hiding</u> under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it ③<u>easily</u>. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at ④<u>random</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ②hiding→hidden: food는 '숨겨진' 것이므로 과거분사 필요. food와 hide는 수동 관계.
det.analysis:
✅ ② hiding → hidden: with + 목적어 + 분사 구문에서 food는 숨겨지는 대상이므로 과거분사
❌ ① compared: compared to = ~와 비교하여, 분사구문 올바름
❌ ③ easily: 부사, found를 수식 올바름
❌ ④ random: at random = 무작위로, 관용 표현 올바름
det.tip: with + O + p.p.(수동): food가 숨겨진 상태. hiding(능동)이면 food가 스스로 숨는 것이 됨

questions.passage: To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device ①<u>what</u> required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees ②<u>knew</u>, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually ③<u>failed</u> to get the food. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much ④<u>better</u> than the chimpanzees.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①what→which: 선행사 a device가 있으므로 관계대명사 which. what은 선행사 포함.
det.analysis:
✅ ① what → which: 선행사 a device 뒤 관계대명사 which 필요. what은 선행사 없이 사용
❌ ② knew: 과거시제 올바름
❌ ③ failed: failed to V 올바름
❌ ④ better: much + 비교급 올바름
det.tip: which vs what: 선행사가 있으면 which, 선행사가 없으면 what. what = the thing which

questions.passage: Neanderthals ①<u>were</u> able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens ②<u>who</u> ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation, while Neanderthals ③<u>tended</u> to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage, allowing them to adapt to an ④<u>ever-change</u> environment.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ever-change→ever-changing: 명사 environment를 수식하는 현재분사 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ ever-change → ever-changing: 형용사 역할의 현재분사 필요. 'ever-changing environment' = 끊임없이 변화하는 환경
❌ ① were: 주어 Neanderthals(복수) 올바름
❌ ② who: 강조구문 'it was ~ who' 올바름
❌ ③ tended: tend to V 올바름
det.tip: ever-changing(현재분사 형용사): 항상 변화하는. 복합형용사 ever- + V-ing 패턴

questions.passage: A successful presentation relies on employing various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures, making natural eye contact, and speaking with an appropriate volume. But just as important, well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively __________ your message. Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 잘 디자인된 슬라이드는 메시지를 효과적으로 전달하는(conveying) 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conveying: 전달하다 — 프레젠테이션 슬라이드의 목적
❌ ② ignoring: 무시하다 — 반대
❌ ③ concealing: 숨기다 — 반대
❌ ④ distorting: 왜곡하다 — 반대
det.tip: convey a message = 메시지를 전달하다. play a critical role in ~ing = ~하는 데 중요한 역할을 하다

questions.passage: First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides ①<u>simple</u>. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to focus more on ②<u>listening</u> than on reading. Next, prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. Lastly, enhance your slides with high-quality images that ③<u>complement</u> the text. By following these simple tips, you can create effective slides that hold your audience's interest and keep them ④<u>distracted</u> from start to finish!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④distracted(산만한)→engaged(집중하는): 청중을 처음부터 끝까지 '집중하게' 해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ distracted(산만한)가 부적절 → 원문은 engaged(참여시키는/집중하게 하는)
❌ ① simple: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② listening: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ complement: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: engaged(집중하는/참여하는) ↔ distracted(산만한). 문맥: 효과적 슬라이드 = 청중 집중

questions.passage: He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures.
questions.stem: Brian Hare의 실험에서 개는 인간의 제스처를 따라 음식을 쉽게 찾았다.

det.korean: 개는 음식이 있는 컵을 가리키자 쉽게 찾았다.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 'the dogs found it easily'로 명확히 일치
❌ F: 원문과 일치하므로 거짓이 아님
det.tip: 원문 직접 대조: dogs → found it easily / wolves → chose cups at random

questions.passage: When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner.
questions.stem: 침팬지는 새로운 파트너와 짝을 이루었을 때에도 음식을 나눠 먹었다.

det.korean: 침팬지는 새 파트너와 짝지어졌을 때 보통 실패했고, 가끔 성공해도 음식을 나누지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 'did not share the food with their partner'로 음식을 나누지 않음
❌ T: 원문과 반대
det.tip: 핵심: chimpanzees + new partners = failed OR did not share. bonobos와의 대비 포인트

questions.passage: Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders.
questions.stem: 호모 사피엔스는 네안데르탈인보다 신체적으로 우월했다.

det.korean: 네안데르탈인이 호모 사피엔스보다 신체적으로 우월했다 (반대).
det.analysis:
✅ F: 'Neanderthals were physically superior to Homo sapiens'이므로 주어가 반대
❌ T: 원문은 네안데르탈인이 우월하다고 함
det.tip: 주의: 주어 뒤바꿈 함정. Neanderthals > Homo sapiens (물리적), Homo sapiens > Neanderthals (사회적)

questions.passage: Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their __________, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. The bonobos solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그들의 협력적 행동(cooperative behavior)을 연구하기 위해 장치를 설치했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ cooperative behavior: 두 개체가 함께 줄을 당기는 실험 = 협력 연구
❌ ① physical dominance: 물리적 지배 — 실험과 무관
❌ ② genetic similarity: 유전적 유사성 — Although절의 내용이지 실험 대상이 아님
❌ ④ territorial control: 영역 통제 — 실험과 무관
det.tip: cooperative behavior = 협력 행동. 실험 설계(두 명이 동시에 줄을 당김)가 단서

ch: kindness is the key to success
questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: __________. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 대안적 관점을 제안한다: 친절이 성공의 열쇠(kindness is the key to success)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② kindness is the key to success: However 뒤 대안적 관점 + 뒤 문장의 kindness 연결
❌ ① aggressive instincts: 글의 주제와 반대
❌ ③ only the strongest can survive: However 앞의 기존 관점이므로 대안이 아님
❌ ④ competition drives all evolution: 글의 주제와 반대
det.tip: However(역접) + alternative view(대안적 관점): 앞 문장의 '강자 생존'과 반대인 '친절 = 성공'

ch: 개와 늑대는 같은 공통 조상을 공유한다.
개의 친화적 본성은 생존 이점을 제공했다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 늑대는 인간의 제스처에 주의를 기울이지 않고 무작위로 컵을 선택했다.
det.analysis:

❌ ① 일치: evolutionary anthropologist
❌ ② 일치: share the same common ancestor
❌ ④ 일치: friendly nature provided them with a survival advantage
det.tip: 내용 불일치 문제: '쉽게 읽었다' vs 원문 '전혀 주의를 기울이지 않았다' — 반대

ch: 네안데르탈인은 도구와 불을 만들 수 있었다.
호모 사피엔스는 더 큰 공동체에 살았다.
네안데르탈인은 호모 사피엔스보다 더 큰 집단에서 살았다.

det.korean: ④ 원문: 네안데르탈인은 더 작은 집단에서 살았다 (smaller groups).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 불일치: 'Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups' → 더 큰 집단이 아님
❌ ① 일치: 'were able to make tools and fire'
❌ ② 일치: 'our ancestors lived in larger communities'
❌ ③ 일치: 'until about 40,000 years ago'

questions.passage: A successful presentation relies on ①<u>employing</u> various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures. ②<u>Well-designing</u> slides play a critical role in effectively conveying your message. ③<u>Limit</u> each slide to five lines of text and use phrases ④<u>instead</u> of full sentences.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법/어휘상 오류가 있는 것은?

det.korean: ②Well-designing→Well-designed: 슬라이드는 '디자인된' 것이므로 과거분사.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Well-designing → Well-designed: slides는 디자인되는 대상(수동)이므로 p.p.
❌ ① employing: relies on ~ing 올바름
❌ ③ Limit: 명령문 올바름
❌ ④ instead of: 전치사구 올바름

Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction. Now let's turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. questions.stem:
위 글을 참고하여, 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: 협력적 특성 없이 보노보는 멸종(extinction)에 직면했을 수 있다.

questions.passage: These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, __________ (allow) them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이러한 사회적 차이가 호모 사피엔스에게 경쟁적 이점을 주어 변화하는 환경에 적응하게(allowing) 했다.
det.analysis: 콤마 뒤 분사구문: 결과를 나타내는 현재분사 allowing. 주어(differences)가 능동적으로 '~하게 하다'
det.tip: 분사구문(결과): ~, allowing them to V = 그래서 그들이 ~할 수 있게 했다

questions.passage: I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as __________, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish.
questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

[ it / adds / the beauty / when / with / the others / harmonizes / each flower / to ]

※ 모두 사용하시오. 대소문자 구분 없음.

det.korean: 각 꽃이 다른 꽃들과 조화를 이룰 때 아름다움에 더하듯이.

ch: 네안데르탈인의 멸종 원인에 대한 새로운 발견
친화적 본성이 생존에 미치는 긍정적 영향
경쟁이 사회 발전의 핵심 동력이라는 주장
questions.passage: It's fascinating how we want to help someone in need. Where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important? Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage. Bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature, and experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. It was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived through cooperation. I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체의 주제: 친화적 본성이 생존에 미치는 긍정적 영향
det.analysis:
✅ ② 친화적 본성이 생존에 미치는 긍정적 영향: 개+보노보+호모사피엔스 모두 협력/친절이 생존의 열쇠
❌ ① 동물 실험의 윤리: 본문 주제가 아님
❌ ③ 네안데르탈인 멸종: 부분적 내용일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님
❌ ④ 경쟁이 핵심: 글의 주제와 반대
det.tip: 글의 핵심 메시지: friendliness/kindness → survival/success. 개, 보노보, 호모사피엔스 세 가지 사례로 증명

ch: 가능한 한 많은 텍스트를 넣어 청중에게 상세한 정보를 제공해야 한다.
슬라이드보다 발표자의 제스처와 목소리가 훨씬 더 중요하다.
글꼴 크기는 중요하지 않으며 색상을 다양하게 사용해야 한다.
슬라이드를 간결하게 유지하고, 가독성을 높이며, 고품질 이미지로 보완해야 한다.
questions.passage: Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. Next, prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally achieved with a font size of at least 18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides with high-quality images that complement the text.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 제시한 효과적인 슬라이드 제작의 핵심 내용을 가장 잘 요약한 것은?

det.korean: ① 간결함(simple) + 가독성(readability) + 고품질 이미지(high-quality images)
det.analysis:
✅ ① 세 가지 팁 정확히 요약: 간결 + 가독성 + 이미지
❌ ② 'less is more'와 정반대
❌ ③ 슬라이드의 중요성을 무시
❌ ④ font size '중요하지 않다'는 원문 반대, 색상 '다양하게'는 원문 반대(3~4색 제한)
det.tip: Deep Learning 지문의 3가지 팁: 1) simple 2) readability 3) high-quality images

accept: communicate and cooperate with different individuals
communicate and cooperate with different individuals.
questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate.

det.analysis: 원문: 'We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals.'
